message.content: {"answer": "C", "option_text": "Figure 1 shows bilateral alveolar-interstitial opacities predominantly in the lung bases, and Figure 4 shows increased alveolar opacities with bilateral consolidations, suggesting rapid progression consistent with alveolar hemorrhage.", "reason": "Visual inspection of Figure 1 reveals diffuse bilateral interstitial markings and subtle basal opacities without dense consolidation. Figure 4 demonstrates a dramatic progression to extensive, dense bilateral alveolar consolidations (ground-glass to white-out appearance), particularly in the mid-to-lower zones. The classifier confirms strong 'Lung Opacity' (0.87) in Figure 4 compared to no strong findings in Figure 1. This pattern of rapidly progressive bilateral airspace disease is characteristic of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage or severe ARDS, matching Option C. Options A, D, and E describe resolution or isolated findings not seen here; Option B suggests nodular formations which are less accurate than the description of confluent consolidation."}
